claims.text: The Act permits decisions to be made despite lack of scientific certainty where relevant scientific information or knowledge is insufficient.

Risk assessment/risk management reporting addresses risks and adverse effects to human, plant and animal health, the environment and biodiversity, together with measures to prevent, reduce or control them.
Emergency response planning is part of the statutory risk-management framework and must provide safety measures/procedures and necessary emergency measures.
The Board may direct organisations conducting modern biotechnology R&D to establish an IBC; the IBC has biosafety oversight functions including procedures and BSL determination for contained-use R&D.
Specified activities require prior notification, with submission arrangements involving the Director General and, where applicable, the IBC.
Notifications are expected to be complete and without errors; the Director General may require amendment, completion or resubmission.
The First Schedule contains contained-use exemptions with specified host/vector systems and criteria; exemption cannot be inferred merely from a generic 'low risk' statement.

Contained-use guidance specifies biosafety-level and work-practice expectations, including access restrictions, training, decontamination and incident controls; GM-BSL2 examples include LMO/materials associated with RG2 microorganisms.
Spills/accidents are to be addressed through established reporting and emergency arrangements, with relevant escalation to supervisory/IBC structures.
A Class II biological safety cabinet is identified for work presenting respiratory/aerosol risk within the applicable contained-use context.
Contained-use guidance covers safe handling, hazardous biological waste treatment, disposal, transfer/transport, storage and minimum facility/equipment requirements.
GMM risk assessment considers hazards, exposure/release, risk controls and BSL assignment, and addresses relevant human, animal, plant and environmental risks.
A defensible risk assessment should contain enough background and detail for reviewers to understand hazards; potential hazards should be acknowledged and uncertainty considered.
Risk assessment should be reviewed and updated as appropriate rather than treated as a one-time unsupported conclusion.

IBC functions include assessment/monitoring of facilities, procedures, practices, training and expertise, containment-level assessment, form completeness, emergency response and reporting of significant incidents/noncompliance.
The PI is accountable to the IBC and must comply with applicable biosafety laws and guidelines.

The IBC guidance specifies incident-reporting routes and timeframes for relevant incidents/occupational exposures; BioSafe should direct users to the applicable institutional/IBC process rather than invent a response.
Form E researcher-facing information includes applicant and responsible scientists/personnel qualifications and experience.
Form E project information includes title, biosafety level, rationale, objectives, schedule/dates and other project particulars specified by the form.
LMO description requires donor/parent organism, vector or method, trait/modified trait, gene identity/function and target information as applicable.
Form E asks for activity-related human-health risks, hazards, likelihood/consequence and risks from unintentional release to human health/environment.
Form E covers transport outside premises and precautions, disposal/decontamination, protection, removal/disposal of exposed organisms, isolation and contingency measures.
Form E includes premises/facility details such as name/type/BSL and relevant inspection/certification/contact/BSO information.
Form E provides for confidential business information claims and justification where applicable.
The IBC Assessment Report is explicitly completed by the registered IBC and is not a researcher/PI field for BioSafe scoring.
The 2023 MOH guideline covers safe transport of clinical specimens and infectious substances, including classification and packaging/labelling/marking requirements.
Basic transport practice uses a triple-packaging concept; the guideline distinguishes relevant Category A/B infectious-substance packaging arrangements including P620/P650 contexts.
The MOH clinical-specimen transport guideline does not serve as the clinical-waste guideline; clinical waste and chemical waste are outside its scope.
SW 404 covers pathogenic wastes, clinical wastes or quarantined materials within the scheduled-waste framework.

Scheduled-waste management includes generator, treatment and disposal obligations; BioSafe should identify the applicable waste stream and verify the prescribed pathway rather than accept generic 'institutional disposal'.
WHO LBM4 uses an evidence- and risk-based approach in which safety measures are balanced against the actual risk of the activity on a case-by-case basis.
Risk assessment requires information on biological hazards, procedures, equipment, facility and human competency; knowledge gaps negatively affect evaluation and control selection.
Risk evaluation considers how exposure/release could occur, likelihood, consequences and whether risks can be controlled to an acceptable level.

WHO's 2024 laboratory biosecurity guidance applies a risk- and evidence-based approach to biosecurity, including governance, secure handling, transport/storage and high-consequence research risk management.

WHO LBM4 includes dedicated guidance on decontamination and waste management; BioSafe should use it as authoritative international corroboration where Malaysian requirements do not fully specify technical practice.

WHO describes biological risk assessment as a systematic process of gathering information and evaluating risks to support risk management. The results of the assessment inform selection of risk control measures, including training and appropriate PPE.

claims.text: In laboratory biosafety, WHO describes a biological hazard as a biological agent whose pathogenic characteristics give it the potential to cause harm to people, animals and/or the environment.
claims.verification_status: Verified against WHO Risk Assessment monograph

claims.text: WHO defines biological risk in context as the combination of the likelihood that an exposure to or release of a biological hazard occurs during laboratory work and the severity of the consequences if that incident occurs.
claims.verification_status: Verified against WHO Risk Assessment monograph

claims.text: WHO notes that laboratory biological risk depends on dynamic factors including the procedures performed, equipment available, pathogenic properties of the biological agent, host range, population susceptibility and the competency of laboratory personnel.
claims.verification_status: Verified against WHO Risk Assessment monograph

claims.section: Step 4 – Select and implement risk control measures
claims.text: WHO risk assessment requires risk control measures to be selected for the specific activity and then considers residual risk and whether the selected measures are available, effective and sustainable.
claims.verification_status: Verified against WHO Risk Assessment monograph

claims.page: Core document overview / risk assessment framework
claims.text: WHO LBM4 uses an evidence- and risk-based approach so that safety measures are balanced against the actual risk of work with biological agents on a case-by-case basis; a proper risk assessment should be performed before activities and should inform risk control measures.
claims.verification_status: Verified against WHO LBM4 core document

claims.text: WHO places PPE within broader laboratory biosafety core requirements rather than treating PPE as a complete safety determination. Core requirements include good microbiological practice and procedure, with PPE such as laboratory coats, footwear, gloves and eye protection used as applicable.

WHO indicates that some PPE needs are determined by risk assessment; for example, respiratory protection for biological agents is not a general core requirement and becomes a heightened control measure when the risk assessment indicates it is needed.

WHO's risk-based framework does not use PPE alone to establish that an activity is safe: risk assessment determines the control measures needed for the activity, and control selection can include training, PPE, equipment and other containment measures appropriate to the identified risk.
claims.verification_status: Verified synthesis of WHO Risk Assessment monograph statements; no new operational procedure added

claims.text: A comprehensive biological risk assessment considers the biological hazard together with how work is performed and the context in which it is performed; relevant information includes procedures, equipment, facility and personnel competency, and the assessment evaluates exposure or release, likelihood and consequences.

retrieval_rules.implementation: For Malaysian legal/regulatory questions, retrieve Tier 1 Malaysia sources before Tier 2/3 sources.
Use current official Malaysian guidance for operational interpretation and Form E assistance.
Use MOH 2023 for clinical specimen/infectious-substance transport; do not use it as the clinical-waste rule.
Use WHO as Tier 3 corroboration or where Malaysian sources do not specify the issue.
Flag need for IBC review; do not simulate or issue an IBC approval and do not score the IBC Assessment Report as a researcher field.
Do not score fee omission or present fees as a BioSafe requirement.
Do not score Annex 2 / IBC Assessment Report as a researcher/PI missing field.
Missing scientific/regulatory facts trigger clarification; never infer organism, construct, BSL, risk group, facility class or transport classification.
Material regulatory conclusions should cite source and section/page when available.
When older procedural material conflicts with a current official operational page, flag reconciliation and prefer the current official operational statement.
BioSafe provides decision support, not an official approval/compliance determination.
Prefer Document → Part/Section → Subsection → Paragraph/claim over arbitrary fixed-size chunks.

BioSafe must not provide actionable instructions that facilitate harmful biological activity. It should identify the safety concern, withhold enabling procedural details, and redirect toward safe biosafety, risk-management, containment, governance, incident-prevention, or other non-enabling institutional guidance.

scope_gates.implementation: Document review, risk identification, regulatory reasoning and researcher-facing Form E support.
BioSafe may identify that IBC review is required but does not reproduce the IBC's assessment role.
Explicit project decision: ignore fee requirements.
Explicit project decision: IBC completes it; not scored as researcher/PI content.
No invented organism, sequence, vector, BSL, risk group or facility classification.
